templates.name: Linux Tools (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/linux/tools.yml -- the first of Robert's 'every playbook gets a Zabbix template' initiative (2026-10-16).

HOW IT WORKS
  One master item reads /etc/example-music/zabbix_status/linux_tools.json via vfs.file.contents every hour. That file is written by linux/tools.yml itself at the end of every run -- Ansible already knows this state from its own tasks (ansible_facts.packages, the update-motd symlink task), so this deliberately does NOT re-derive it a second time via a separate agent-side script. All other items are DEPENDENT on the master and extract fields via JSONPath.

STALENESS
  The {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE} macro (default 2d) drives a nodata() trigger on the master item itself -- catches linux/tools.yml not having run recently at all, not just config drift the report would otherwise go stale on.

IMPORT INSTRUCTIONS
  Zabbix API: configuration.import (rules: createMissing for groups/templates/items/triggers, updateExisting for the rest). Or via the UI: Data collection -> Templates -> Import.
  Link to each Linux host this playbook manages.

NOT YET DONE (flagged, not forgotten)
  Package presence is currently reported by Ansible (missing_packages/_count), not checked natively by the agent via vfs.file.exists per-package -- Robert's own stated preference (checksum-stable dpkg -L copyright paths) fits a native per-package item better long-term, via an LLD discovery rule driven by common_packages rather than this template needing updates every time that list changes. Deferred to the next iteration once this v1 is proven -- the discoveryrule.create/itemprototype.create/triggerprototype.create API shapes haven't been verified yet.

items.name: Linux Tools: status report (master)
items.description: Raw JSON status report written by linux/tools.yml at the end of every run. All other items in this template depend on this one.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: no status report for {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE} on {HOST.NAME} -- linux/tools.yml may not be running
triggers.description: linux/tools.yml hasn't written a fresh status report within {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE}. Either the playbook hasn't run against this host recently, or the zabbix-agent/file path is broken. Check: ls -la /etc/example-music/zabbix_status/linux_tools.json and re-run linux/tools.yml.

items.name: Linux Tools: missing packages count
items.description: Count of common_packages (group_vars/all/main.yml) not currently installed, per the last linux/tools.yml run's own ansible_facts.packages check.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: {ITEM.LASTVALUE} package(s) missing on {HOST.NAME}
triggers.description: One or more packages in common_packages (group_vars/all/main.yml) are not installed. Check the 'Linux Tools: missing packages (list)' item for which ones, then re-run linux/tools.yml.

items.name: Linux Tools: missing packages (list)
items.description: The actual list of missing package names, for diagnosis -- no trigger of its own, see the count item's trigger.

items.name: Linux Tools: update-motd symlink healthy
items.description: 1 if /etc/update-motd.d/98-update-status is a real symlink to /usr/local/bin/update-motd, 0 otherwise.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: update-motd not linked on {HOST.NAME}
triggers.description: The update-motd symlink is missing or broken. Re-run linux/tools.yml -- see its 'Link update-motd into /etc/update-motd.d' task.

macros.description: How long the status report can go without a fresh write before the staleness trigger fires. Override per-host if a host is deliberately on a less frequent Ansible run schedule.
